jobs.title: Senior Director Wealth Management IT Data/AI & BOR
jobs.description:
A career as a Senior Director of Wealth Management IT – Data/AI and BOR at National Bank means acting as a leader, acceleratingtransformation. We are looking for a highly skilledand visionary individual to lead ourwealth management dataand artificial intelligence strategy by driving the delivery of critical solutions, strategic intelligenceand reporting. 
This role includes managing and modernizing the wealth BI and reporting team and ecosystems, overseeing IBOR investment registry operations (including managing tax statements and slips), and modernizing legacy platforms to meet the demands of a rapidly evolving financial services industry.
You act as a field technology leader, having technical expertise, strategic thinking, and leadership skills to transform data capabilities and operations while aligning with business objectives and regulatory standards.

Your job

Define and deploy the wealth management data and AI strategy to improve analytics, decision-making, and automation.
Ensure data governance, security, and quality, while integrating emerging technologies to support innovation and maintain a competitive advantage.
Lead the Wealth Management BI & Reporting team to provide relevant analytics that support business objectives.
Design modern BI solutions, in collaboration with architecture, enabling real-time and self-service analytics.
Define performance indicators (KPIs) and stakeholder needs, in line with the organization's priorities.
Oversee IBOR operations, including the production of customer statements and tax slips, in compliance with regulatory requirements.
Implement and maintain robust processes and technologies to ensure reliable and efficient IBOR operations.
Lead the modernization of IBOR systems to improve their reliability, scalability, and responsiveness to business and compliance needs.
Drive the modernization of data platforms and IBOR systems to cloud-based, scalable and automated solutions.
Define architecture standards with IT teams and ensure the integration of new technologies, while limiting the impact on activities through effective change management.
Lead and mobilize a high-performance IT team, promoting innovation, collaboration and continuous improvement, in partnership with business and technology teams and suppliers.
Lead the delivery of initiatives by managing budgets, timelines and resources, as well as regularly monitoring progress, risks and opportunities with senior management.

Your team

The IT and Operations sector is made up of more than 5500 experts who work in an agile, proactive and collaborative manner to seize opportunities, stay on the cutting edge of technology and continuously improve processes.
Within the IT Wealth Management Delivery sector, you are part of a large team and report to the Vice President, IT Wealth Management. This role will allow you to lead transformative initiatives at the intersection of data, AI and wealth management. You will work with cutting-edge technologies and drive impactful innovations.
You benefit from a hybrid work model with a required presence in the office three days a week (minimum) and the option to work remotely the other two days, promoting both in-person collaboration and flexibility.
The Bank values continuous development and internal mobility. Our personalized training programs, based on learning in action, allow you to master your craft and develop new areas of expertise. Tools such as the Data Academy, language training, the Harvard Learning Center and coaching and mentoring support are available to you at all times.
Prerequisites

Bachelor's degree in computer science, software engineering, artificial intelligence, data science or related technology field or any other combination of education and experience deemed equivalent
10 years of relevant experience in IT leadership, with a focus on data strategy, AI and business systems management, including manager management.
Strong experience in data strategy, AI technologies and modern BI/reporting platforms (databricks, snowflake)
Experience with Investment Registry Systems and Operations (IBOR), including tax and regulatory reporting.
Experience in modernizing legacy systems and implementing cloud-based, AI-driven, and data-centric solutions.
Knowledge of data governance, regulatory compliance, and risk management in the wealth management space.
Demonstrated ability to lead and inspire cross-functional teams.
Experience in the wealth management or financial services industry is an asset. 

Languages: French, English
Reason to require this language: you will need to work closely with our colleagues outside Quebec.
Required skills: Artificial Intelligence, Business Alignment, Collaboration, Communication, Cybersecurity, Decision Making, Emotional Intelligence, Initiative, Managerial Courage, Mobilization, Problem Solving, Strategy Execution, Team Alignment, Technical Leadership, User-centered Design

Your benefits

In addition to competitive compensation, upon hiring you’ll be eligible for a wide range of flexible benefits to help promote your wellbeing and that of your family such as:

* Health and wellness program, including many options
* Flexible group insurance
* Generous pension plan
* Employee Share Ownership Plan
* Employee and family assistance program
* Preferential banking services
* Involvement in community initiatives
* Telemedicine service
* Virtual sleep clinic

We have an offer that keeps up with trends as well as your needs and those of your family.

Our dynamic work environments and cutting-edge collaboration tools foster a positive employee experience. We value employees’ ideas. Whether through our surveys or programs, regular feedback and ongoing communication are encouraged.

Making a bold move in a people-first environment

We’re a bank on a human scale that stands out for its courage, entrepreneurial culture, and passion for people. Our mission is to have a positive impact on people’s lives. Our core values of partnership, agility, and empowerment inspire us, and inclusion is central to our commitments. We aim, wherever possible, to provide a barrier-free and accessible environment to all employees.

We strive to provide accessibility measures throughout the recruitment process within the limits of our available resources. If you require accommodations, feel free to let us know during our initial conversations. We welcome all candidates! What can you bring to our team?

Join us!

jobs.title: Senior Director, Commercial Finance & Performance Management (CFPM)
jobs.description:
Company:

Finning International Inc.

Number of Openings:

1

Worker Type:

Permanent

Position Overview:

Finning Canada is hiring a Permanent, Full-time Senior Director, Commercial Finance & Performance Management (CFPM), based in either Edmonton or Calgary.

Reporting to the Vice President, Finance & Supply Chain, this role represents one of the most senior and influential finance leadership positions within Finning Canada. As the senior commercial finance leader for a ~$6B revenue business, the Senior Director, CFPM plays a pivotal role in driving profitable growth, optimizing capital deployment, and strengthening commercial governance across the organization. Partnering closely with Canadian Operations, this leader oversees the Commercial & Financial Business Partnering team and serves as a trusted advisor to senior and executive leadership, translating strategy into actionable financial insight.

Leading a high-performing team of finance leaders, the role champions strong commercial acumen, best-in-class budgeting, forecasting, and strategic planning, and delivers insightful financial and operational reporting to enable data-driven decision-making and effective performance management. With significant exposure to the Canadian leadership team and the broader Finning Executive, this role offers the opportunity to lead high-impact initiatives, influence enterprise-wide strategy, and shape the financial future of the business. Positioned as a key succession role to the VP, Finance & Supply Chain, this role provides a clear pathway to broader executive accountability and long-term leadership growth within Finning.

Job Description:

Major Job Functions:

Strategic & Commercial Leadership

Drive financial strategy aligned to Finning and Caterpillar objectives
Provide executive decision support and investment governance
Identify competitive trends and growth opportunities
Operate with integrity through maintaining social, ethical and organizational integrity in conducting business activities; maintains confidentiality, adheres to corporate policies and procedures
Accountable for the Commercial Governance for Finning Canada. $6Bn+ of revenue, $500M of EBIT
Accountable for delivering the strategic plan, governance processes and alignment internally with Finning and Caterpillar
Accountable to be a change agent in how we manage and re-shape the business

Drive Financial Performance across the business

Leader in driving, understanding and analysing financial performance on a monthly, quarterly and annual basis
Owner of identifying gaps in performance and implementing action plans to address
Take an objective view, balancing operational and corporate requirements
Identify, communicate, and mitigate potential issues or liabilities; recommend effective solutions
Focus on EBIT, Invested Capital, ROIC and FCF

Financial Planning, Analysis & Reporting

Own budgeting, forecasting, and long‑range plans
Responsible for the efficient management of financial and accounting operations including financial reporting, budgeting, asset management and control
Provide financially sound information and manage the effective flow of that information through financial systems, reports, and dashboards
Ensure high‑quality C‑suite reporting and KPI insight
Improve forecast accuracy and performance analytics

Governance & Capital Discipline

Lead large deal/tender governance and post‑investment review
Approve major commercial decisions and business cases

Leadership & Stakeholder Influence

Act as trusted advisor to the FINCA EC, FLT, and Board
Represent FINCA with Caterpillar and external stakeholders
Lead the CFPM Team, driving engagement, development talent and providing a succession pipeline
100% accountability for results and impact on people by setting a strong example in high performance leadership

Education and Qualifications:

10+ years of relevant industry experience is required
10+ years experience in a leadership capacity
10+ years of progressive accounting experience in related industry or public practice.
Master's or Bachelor’s degree in finance or related degree preferred
Accounting designation or graduate degree preferred
Highly effective senior leadership skills gained through previous leadership experience
Experience leading implementation projects for financial systems at a senior leader level, on a global scale (system examples: BPC, SAP, Hyperion, M3, Peoplesoft, or Other)
Practical experience and theoretical knowledge in Dealership Business Models, end-to-end supply chain management and Financial & Commercial practices
Operational experience across a number of disciplines / functions
Global business strategy and corporate finance knowledge
Advanced general accounting knowledge coupled with a sound understanding of business processes, the interrelationship of business functions, corporate governance issues and operational needs
Knowledge of financial systems with historical proven, positive track record of solution implementation, optimization, and sustainment
Knowledge of the operations of related industry segments
Proficient in the use of MS Office Suite and in-house systems including BPC, M3, Power BI, Concur
Understands and adheres to Finning policies and procedures, including safety, inclusion, and diversity
Ability to determine key performance indicators (KPIs), variance issues and improve internal controls
Experience working with CAT systems, tools, data, or reports including DFRS, CAT dealer portal is preferred
Change management training, experience, and/or PROSCI or Lean Change Agent certification preferred

Soft Skills:

Strong team leadership skills, capable of representing the business at a senior management level with robust stakeholder management.
Effective verbal communication skills, presenting messages clearly, concisely, and directly.
Influencing skills, ability to drive results without direct line responsibility and ensure the wider team are engaged and effective.
Strong Analytical / Problem solving attributes. Ability to Design, interrogate and review Financial and Operational information and create clear and effective understanding with stakeholders.
Advanced Commercial acumen with the ability to drive improvements in financial returns and profitability.
Ability to clearly articulate the value of financial analysis, linked to business results
Must possess highest standard of accuracy and precision and be highly organized
Self motivated and results oriented, with a desire to achieve
Ability to deal with ambiguity and assist in creating sustainable competitive advantage
Effective change management capabilities
Professional, timely and accurate presentation of information
Ability to continuously learn and develop role related skills
Ability to manage, motivate and develop a large and diverse team

We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and we actively encourage all individuals to express themselves and achieve their full potential. As a company, we continuously strive to enhance our outreach to individuals of all backgrounds and identities. Furthermore, Finning is committed to collaborating with and providing reasonable accommodations /adjustments to individuals with disabilities. jobs.title: Director, Engineering and Procurement, AI Fabric
jobs.description:
Req Id:
432862

Connection is everything. It drives us to innovate, explore, and stay close to what matters to us most. At Bell, we’re building a more connected future through world-class networks, AI-powered solutions, and digital experiences that elevate how people live, work, and play every day.

We believe in empowering people. That’s why we equip our teams with cutting-edge technology, AI tools, and a collaborative environment that supports creativity and growth. Want to be part of a diverse team where your work makes a real impact? If you’re inspired by innovation that advances how people connect and transforms what’s possible, you belong on #TeamBell.

On the Bell Business Markets team, you’ll be a vital part of making innovation happen for enterprise-scale customers. You’ll deliver advanced solutions in areas such as IoT, Mobility/5G, Cloud, Cyber Security, Voice, Collaboration & Contact Centre and Internet & Private Networks.

At Bell, your skills and expertise will help set us apart as we continue to be the leading provider of digital connections and next generation services to businesses and governments.

Summary

Bell's AI Fabric initiative is building Canada's largest sovereign AI infrastructure platform, comprising seven large-scale, high-density data centres across the country, including a 500 MW British Columbia supercluster and a future 1.2 GW flagship campus in Regina, Saskatchewan.

Reporting to the VP, Capital Programs, the Director, Engineering & Procurement is responsible for providing leadership across engineering governance, technical strategy, strategic sourcing, procurement, and supplier management for Bell's national AI Fabric portfolio. This role will lead multidisciplinary engineering teams while overseeing the procurement of mission-critical infrastructure, ensuring Bell secures and delivers the power, cooling, electrical, mechanical, network, and modular systems required to support hyperscale AI operations. Working closely with Construction, Program Controls, Commissioning, Operations, Finance, Legal, and external partners, the Director will drive engineering excellence, commercial value, supply chain resilience, and successful project execution across a multi-billion-dollar capital program.

Key Responsibilities

Lead the engineering and procurement functions supporting Bell AI Fabric developments across multiple Canadian sites.
Establish engineering standards, technical specifications, design governance processes, and quality assurance frameworks for mission-critical infrastructure.
Oversee engineering reviews and approvals for power distribution, utility interconnections, backup generation, UPS systems, cooling infrastructure, liquid cooling technologies, controls, and related systems.
Develop and execute procurement strategies for major capital equipment, engineering services, and long-lead infrastructure components required for AI data centre development.
Lead supplier selection, commercial negotiations, contract management, and strategic partnerships with OEMs, engineering firms, utilities, EPC contractors, and technology vendors.
Drive capacity planning, infrastructure resiliency, technology roadmaps, and technical risk mitigation strategies supporting high-density AI and GPU workloads.
Partner with Construction, Commissioning, Operations, and Program Controls teams to ensure engineering and procurement activities align with project schedules, budgets, and operational requirements.
Manage supply chain risks, supplier performance, cost optimization initiatives, and procurement governance across the portfolio.
Provide executive-level recommendations regarding infrastructure investments, commercial strategies, engineering risks, and project delivery performance.
Develop and lead a high-performing team while fostering a culture of safety, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement.

Critical Qualifications

12+ years of progressive leadership experience in engineering, procurement, construction, mission-critical facilities, data centres, energy infrastructure, or large-scale capital programs.
5+ years of people leadership experience managing engineering, procurement, project delivery, or integrated infrastructure teams.
Demonstrated experience delivering hyperscale data centres, mission-critical facilities, utility infrastructure, or large-scale industrial construction projects.
Strong technical expertise in electrical distribution systems, cooling infrastructure, liquid cooling technologies, resiliency design, and mission-critical operations.
Proven success leading strategic sourcing initiatives, complex commercial negotiations, and major procurement programs.
Deep understanding of engineering governance, capital project delivery, EPC contracting models, procurement practices, and commissioning processes.
Strong financial and commercial acumen, including budget management, forecasting, business case development, and contract administration.
Exceptional stakeholder management, communication, negotiation, and executive presentation skills.
Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Civil, Construction Engineering, or a related technical discipline; P.Eng. designation strongly preferred.
Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, high-growth environment and travel as required to support projects across Canada.

Adequate knowledge of French is required for positions in Quebec.

Management

Canada : Alberta : Calgary

jobs.description:
Who are we?

Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.

A place where bold ideas are welcomed, human connection is valued, and everyone has the opportunity to shape their future.

A career at Equinix means being at the center of shaping what comes next and amplifying customer value through innovation and impact. You’ll work across teams, influence key decisions, and help shape the path forward. You’ll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes you—because when you feel valued, you’re empowered to do your best work.

Job Summary

The Vice President, Finance Transformation is a strategic executive leader responsible for driving the modernization and optimization of the Finance organization. This role leads a centralized team of transformation experts charged with designing and executing enterprise-wide finance initiatives that improve operating effectiveness, organizational scalability, processes, systems, data, and ways of working.

The Vice President, Finance Transformation serves as a key advisor to the Chief Financial Officer and Finance Leadership Team, translating strategic priorities into actionable transformation programs. This leader will oversee initiatives including organizational design, location and workforce strategy, shared services optimization, technology enablement, automation, artificial intelligence adoption, process excellence, governance, and change management to build a world-class Finance function.

Responsibilities

Finance Transformation Strategy

Develop and lead the multi-year Finance Transformation roadmap aligned to business and Finance objectives
Partner with the Chief Financial Officer and Finance Leadership Team to identify opportunities to improve efficiency, scalability, agility, and decision-making capabilities
Establish transformation priorities, business cases, milestones, and success metrics
Drive cross-functional alignment and executive sponsorship for major transformation initiatives

Organizational and Operating Model Excellence

Lead Finance organizational redesign efforts, including workforce planning, role optimization, and operating model evolution
Develop global location strategies, including shared services, centers of excellence, and hub-based delivery models, and oversee execution
Evaluate and implement organizational structures that improve efficiency and talent utilization
Ensure Finance capabilities are aligned with future business needs

Process Optimization and Continuous Improvement

Champion process standardization and simplification across all Finance functios
Implement best-in-class operating practices and continuous improvement methodologies
Identify opportunities to reduce complexity, improve controls, and enhance service delivery
Establish governance models that drive accountability and measurable outcomes

Technology and Digital Transformation

Partner with Finance Systems, Information Technology, and business stakeholders to develop and manage a multi-year roadmap to modernize Finance technology platforms
Oversee implementation and optimization of planning, reporting, consolidation, enterprise resource planning, automation, and analytics tools
Lead adoption of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, machine learning, data automation, and advanced analytics capabilities
Ensure Finance technology investments deliver measurable business value

Program Management and Change Leadership

Build and lead a high-performing transformation office responsible for delivering strategic initiatives
Establish rigorous program management disciplines, including prioritization, governance, risk management, and benefits tracking
Lead organization-wide change management efforts supporting transformation adoption
Foster a culture of innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement

Stakeholder Management

Serve as a trusted advisor to Finance executives and key business partners
Coordinate transformation efforts across Finance, Human Resources, Information Technology, Operations, and Corporate Functions
Provide regular updates to executive leadership regarding transformation progress, risks, and outcomes

Qualifications

Required Experience

Proven years of progressive experience in Finance, Consulting, Business Transformation, or Operational Excellence roles
Proven years leading large-scale transformation initiatives within complex organizations
Demonstrated success driving Finance operating model, process, and technology transformations
Experience leading enterprise programs involving multiple stakeholders and executive-level sponsors
Strong people leadership experience, including building and developing high-performing teams

Preferred Experience

Background in management consulting, corporate transformation, or finance strategy
Experience with enterprise resource planning, planning, and finance technology implementations
Experience developing global location and shared services strategies
MBA, CPA, CMA, or equivalent advanced business credential preferred

Competencies

Demonstrates strategic thinking and an enterprise mindset
Builds credibility as a trusted advisor and influences executive stakeholders effectively
Leads large-scale organizational change with clarity, discipline, and accountability
Collaborates effectively across functions, geographies, and levels of the organization
Establishes rigorous program governance and drives execution excellence
Uses data and measurable outcomes to inform decisions and track business value
Builds, develops, and inspires high-performing teams

We are dedicated to offering our customers the highest quality products and services and are looking for people with the inspiration and talent to develop with us as we pursue our ambitious growth strategy. We are a leader in developing state-of-the-art technology and it is this technology base that uniquely positions us to serve customers who seek differentiation through solutions that provide speed, flexibility and maximum productivity. This capability is at the core of our mission and competitive strategy.

Husky TechnologiesTM offers a wealth of opportunity for personal growth and development. Most importantly, Husky Technologies TM offers an opportunity to work with – and be challenged by – a team of great people. Position Overview:

Finning Canada is hiring a Permanent, Full-time Senior Director, Commercial Finance & Performance Management (CFPM), based in either Edmonton or Calgary.

Reporting to the Vice President, Finance & Supply Chain, this role represents one of the most senior and influential finance leadership positions within Finning Canada. As the senior commercial finance leader for a ~$6B revenue business, the Senior Director, CFPM plays a pivotal role in driving profitable growth, optimizing capital deployment, and strengthening commercial governance across the organization. Partnering closely with Canadian Operations, this leader oversees the Commercial & Financial Business Partnering team and serves as a trusted advisor to senior and executive leadership, translating strategy into actionable financial insight.

Leading a high-performing team of finance leaders, the role champions strong commercial acumen, best-in-class budgeting, forecasting, and strategic planning, and delivers insightful financial and operational reporting to enable data-driven decision-making and effective performance management. With significant exposure to the Canadian leadership team and the broader Finning Executive, this role offers the opportunity to lead high-impact initiatives, influence enterprise-wide strategy, and shape the financial future of the business. Positioned as a key succession role to the VP, Finance & Supply Chain, this role provides a clear pathway to broader executive accountability and long-term leadership growth within Finning.

Job Description:

Major Job Functions:

Strategic & Commercial Leadership

Drive financial strategy aligned to Finning and Caterpillar objectives
Provide executive decision support and investment governance
Identify competitive trends and growth opportunities
Operate with integrity through maintaining social, ethical and organizational integrity in conducting business activities; maintains confidentiality, adheres to corporate policies and procedures
Accountable for the Commercial Governance for Finning Canada. $6Bn+ of revenue, $500M of EBIT
Accountable for delivering the strategic plan, governance processes and alignment internally with Finning and Caterpillar
Accountable to be a change agent in how we manage and re-shape the business

Drive Financial Performance across the business

Leader in driving, understanding and analysing financial performance on a monthly, quarterly and annual basis
Owner of identifying gaps in performance and implementing action plans to address
Take an objective view, balancing operational and corporate requirements
Identify, communicate, and mitigate potential issues or liabilities; recommend effective solutions
Focus on EBIT, Invested Capital, ROIC and FCF

Financial Planning, Analysis & Reporting

Own budgeting, forecasting, and long‑range plans
Responsible for the efficient management of financial and accounting operations including financial reporting, budgeting, asset management and control
Provide financially sound information and manage the effective flow of that information through financial systems, reports, and dashboards
Ensure high‑quality C‑suite reporting and KPI insight
Improve forecast accuracy and performance analytics

Governance & Capital Discipline

Lead large deal/tender governance and post‑investment review
Approve major commercial decisions and business cases

Leadership & Stakeholder Influence

Act as trusted advisor to the FINCA EC, FLT, and Board
Represent FINCA with Caterpillar and external stakeholders
Lead the CFPM Team, driving engagement, development talent and providing a succession pipeline
100% accountability for results and impact on people by setting a strong example in high performance leadership

Education and Qualifications:

10+ years of relevant industry experience is required
10+ years experience in a leadership capacity
10+ years of progressive accounting experience in related industry or public practice.
Master's or Bachelor’s degree in finance or related degree preferred
Accounting designation or graduate degree preferred
Highly effective senior leadership skills gained through previous leadership experience
Experience leading implementation projects for financial systems at a senior leader level, on a global scale (system examples: BPC, SAP, Hyperion, M3, Peoplesoft, or Other)
Practical experience and theoretical knowledge in Dealership Business Models, end-to-end supply chain management and Financial & Commercial practices
Operational experience across a number of disciplines / functions
Global business strategy and corporate finance knowledge
Advanced general accounting knowledge coupled with a sound understanding of business processes, the interrelationship of business functions, corporate governance issues and operational needs
Knowledge of financial systems with historical proven, positive track record of solution implementation, optimization, and sustainment
Knowledge of the operations of related industry segments
Proficient in the use of MS Office Suite and in-house systems including BPC, M3, Power BI, Concur
Understands and adheres to Finning policies and procedures, including safety, inclusion, and diversity
Ability to determine key performance indicators (KPIs), variance issues and improve internal controls
Experience working with CAT systems, tools, data, or reports including DFRS, CAT dealer portal is preferred
Change management training, experience, and/or PROSCI or Lean Change Agent certification preferred

Soft Skills:

Strong team leadership skills, capable of representing the business at a senior management level with robust stakeholder management.
Effective verbal communication skills, presenting messages clearly, concisely, and directly.
Influencing skills, ability to drive results without direct line responsibility and ensure the wider team are engaged and effective.
Strong Analytical / Problem solving attributes. Ability to Design, interrogate and review Financial and Operational information and create clear and effective understanding with stakeholders.
Advanced Commercial acumen with the ability to drive improvements in financial returns and profitability.
Ability to clearly articulate the value of financial analysis, linked to business results
Must possess highest standard of accuracy and precision and be highly organized
Self motivated and results oriented, with a desire to achieve
Ability to deal with ambiguity and assist in creating sustainable competitive advantage
Effective change management capabilities
Professional, timely and accurate presentation of information

jobs.description:
Overview

to join our dynamic team in Montreal.

Our IT audit service lines include

Assisting KPMG Audit teams in both audit of technology and in leveraging technology in financial statement audits and integrated audits of financial statements and internal controls. Audit technology-related risks and controls and assist our Audit teams in addressing complex technology topics, including impacts of client artificial intelligence (AI) usage on the audits. Also, perform system implementation assessments in support of external audits at our clients.
Formal assurance on systems, processes, and controls, including Audits of Service Organization Controls (i.e., SOC 1 engagements under CSAE 3416, SSAE 18, and/or ISAE 3402), SOC 2 and SOC 3 engagements (systems security & reliability assurance), and other standards.

What You Will Do

Working closely with our Audit teams as the IT executive in charge for some client where permissible to scope processes, conducting assessments of IT risks and controls, including general IT controls and automated controls embedded within information systems in support of our external audit engagements.
Overseeing, conducting IT audit procedures (e.g., IT risk assessments, General IT Controls, IT Application Controls, large System Implementations and Data Conversions) in support of financial statement audits and internal controls over financial reporting.
Overseeing, conducting IT internal audit and third-party attestation engagements such as CSAE 3416 / SSAE 18 / SOC 1 and SOC 2 reports.
Overseeing the planning, managing, and completing IT Audit project tasks including liaising with client and KPMG teams; collecting, testing, and exploring information; documenting and evaluating IT processes, controls, policies, strategies; and performing detailed quality assurance review and feedback on the work of others.
Communicating (written and verbal) findings and recommendations to the client including technical and business communication to management through the preparation of reports and analyses; preparation of advisory and assurance reports and related deliverables.
Guiding field engagement teams as well as coaching junior staff members.
Influencing and contributing to other practice initiatives, including but not limited to knowledge sharing, training, HR initiatives, and practice management activities.
Supporting regulators file inspections process.
Supporting go-to-market initiatives for business development.

What You Bring To The Role

Bachelor’s degree (or higher) in Business or Computer Science degree required, ideally with a major in accounting.
Completion of one or a combination of the following designations CA, CISA, CISSP.
Minimum of 10 years of combined relevant experience in IT Audit (internal and/or external audit) within a large consulting practice.
Strong understanding and experience with IT Integrated Audits and controls-based audits
Strong understanding and experience with third-party assurance reports (e.g., CSAE 3416, SSAE 18, SOC 2) is required.
Experience with the identification and or evaluation of process level controls in large system transformation projects involving SAP and or Oracle.
Experience in the testing of controls in different IT environments, like SAP, Oracle, Unix, Linux, AS400, Mainframe, etc.
Experience within an external audit practice auditing client in the Financial Services, Technology and Telecom, and Mining industry.
Ability to work both, with little supervision and within a team environment.
Excellent communication skills being able to express insights, both written and orally.
Demonstrated ability to learn and succeed in a fast-paced environment.
Attention to detail and strong organization and investigative skills.
Strong understanding of business risks and audit risks.
Have a high degree of personal confidence, enthusiasm, and drive.

This position requires written and oral fluency in English because it involves interpretation and application of English standards, guidance, laws and regulations, servicing of English-speaking clients located across Canada and collaboration with English Speaking colleagues located outside of Quebec.

Providing you with the support you need to be at your best

Our Values, The KPMG Way

Integrity
, we do what is right | Excellence
, we never stop learning and improving | Courage
, we think and act boldly | Together
, we respect each other and draw strength from our differences | For Better
, we do what matters

KPMG in Canada is a proud equal opportunities employer and we are committed to creating a respectful, inclusive and barrier-free workplace that allows all of our people to reach their full potential. A diverse workforce is key to our success and we believe in bringing your whole self to work. We welcome all qualified candidates to apply and hope you will choose KPMG in Canada as your employer of choice.

Adjustments and accommodations throughout the recruitment process

At KPMG, we are committed to fostering an inclusive recruitment process where all candidates can be themselves and excel. We aim to provide a positive experience and are prepared to offer adjustments or accommodations to help you perform at your best. Adjustments (informal requests), such as extra preparation time or the option for micro breaks during interviews, and accommodations (formal requests), such as accessible communication supports or technology aids, are tailored to individual needs and role requirements. You will have an opportunity to request an adjustment or accommodation at any point throughout the recruitment process. If you require support, please contact KPMG’s Employee Relations Service team by calling 1-888-466-4778.

AI Usage

We embrace the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to enhance the candidate experience and streamline our recruitment processes. AI tools may help with organizing applications or surfacing relevant qualifications. However, no hiring decisions are made using AI. Every hiring decision is made by our hiring managers and recruitment professionals, who are equipped with training that empowers them to use these tools responsibly. AI technologies used in our recruitment process undergo detailed risk assessments, including security and privacy requirements, that align with KPMG’s Trusted AI framework.

We believe technology should empower human judgment, not replace it. It’s one of the many ways we’re delivering on our vision of being a technology-first, people-driven firm.
